atTheLatestLook: at the latest look: {n}, the most at once: {most}
networkLoss: Network loss on the way to the server
networkLossAbout: The monitor's requests to this server have to be sent again too often: packets are lost on the way to it. Every loss holds a request back by 0.2 s or more; viewers on the same way lose packets just so.
networkLossWhy: More than 5 % of the requests to the server in five minutes needed a TCP retransmission. The incident goes on until the share is below 2.5 %.
noFiguresWereSavedForThis: No figures were saved for this incident: it started before details were introduced, or the check does not provide them.
noOpenIncidentsOfTheSelected: No open incidents of the selected levels
ofServersHint: The same problem on several streams of a server at once, or loss on the way to it
scopeAll: Every vantage point saw the problem ({names}): it arises before their paths part, at the source or the packager.
scopeElsewhere: Streams served by other servers had the same problem at the same time too ({n} of them).
scopeOnlyThis: Only {agent} saw the problem; {names} did not at the same time. The likely cause is on the path of that vantage point: its network or the server that answers it.
scopeServerAlone: No other stream served by {server} had this problem at the time: the cause is most likely the stream itself or its source.
scopeServerOne: One more stream served by {server} had the same problem at the same time. That is not enough to blame the server.
scopeServerWide: Other streams served by {server} had the same problem at the same time ({n} of them): the cause is most likely that server, not the stream.
scopeSingle: The stream is checked from one vantage point, so there is nothing to compare with. A second one would tell whether the source or the delivery is at fault.
scopeSome: {seen} saw the problem, {clear} did not: it depends on where the request comes from and which server answers it.
scopeTitle: Where to look for the cause
serverEpisodes: Began {n} times; the pauses in between add up to {idle}.
thereWereNoIncidentsOfThe: There were no incidents of the selected levels
timesHint: The problem went away and came back within ten minutes: it is one incident. The duration leaves out the pauses in between.
whyTheServersText: The same problem was there at once on several streams this server answered for (up to {n} at a time). With three or more, the cause is more likely the server than the streams.
